title: `eval` runs a string as code in the host's own scope, so no row can describe it and the operation is refused; the name still resolves
notes: THIS CASE REPLACES `eval-is-usable-and-not-forbidden`, AND IT CONTRADICTS A LOCKED SPECIFICATION SENTENCE ON PURPOSE. That sentence is `specification/compatibility.mdx` §Dynamic Features: '`any` and `eval` remain usable. General Smithers guidance may lint against them; the language does not forbid them.' The replaced case pinned exactly that: `eval("1 + 1")` compiled and printed `2`. **`compatibility.mdx` §Dynamic Features needs amending, and until it is, this case is ahead of the specification. It is recorded in `poc/PRODUCTION_READINESS.md` as an open decision.** WHY THE CHANGE WAS MADE ANYWAY: two `MUST`s in the same document were being violated, measured, on both backends. `compatibility.mdx:36` — 'Platform-specific globals such as `process`, `window`, `document`, filesystem, and network MUST NOT be unconditional globals in authored `.sm` code' — and `:38` — 'Host-sensitive operations such as clock and random access MUST still use capabilities.' Measured before the fix: `Date.now()` was refused `SMITHERS1602`, while `eval("Date.now()")` reported `ok: true` with `failures: []` and `requirements: []` and RAN; `eval("process.platform")` returned the host platform on both backends with zero diagnostics; `eval("Math.random()")` bypassed `SMITHERS1603`. Twenty of twenty-two measured spellings failed open, including a shorthand `{ eval }` and `Function.prototype.constructor`. A `MUST NOT` outranks a permission, so the escape was closed and the permissive sentence is the one that has to move. WHAT THE RULE ACTUALLY IS, and why it is narrower than 'eval is forbidden': the **name** still resolves and is not refused — `Function` remains a usable type and `x instanceof Function` remains a prototype test — while every **operation** that reaches the callee through a read is refused. That is not a new shape: `crypto` is already exactly this in the same file, absent from `UNIVERSAL_GLOBALS`, its name unrefused, its every use refused. So a defensible reading of the locked sentence survives — `eval` is not forbidden as an identifier — but that reading is thinner than the sentence's plain meaning and should not be assumed without ratification. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the message text, which names the reasoning ('the enclosing row cannot describe what it reads, throws, or requires') and may be reworded. Its sibling `18-typescript-requirement/any-is-usable-and-not-forbidden` is untouched and still passes: the `any` half of that specification sentence is unaffected, because `any` cannot reach the host namespace by itself. Position is line 5 column 13, the `eval` read inside the template substitution — the read, not the call, because every measured escape reaches the callee through a read.
